author: Obit Feed
title: Captain Patrick J. Thompson
text:
Captain Patrick J Thompson St. Augustine, FL – Patrick J. Thompson of Anastasia Island, Florida, passed away peacefully on August 31, 2026, following a long illness.
Patrick was born in Chelsea, Massachusetts, the son of June and Jim Thompson, and grew up in Niskayuna, New York. From an early age, he was known for his strength, determination, and competitive spirit. A successful high school football and track athlete, Patrick earned the nickname "The Rock," a name that stayed with him well into his early adult years and, in many ways, reflected the man he would become.
After attending Saint Joseph's University in Indiana for a year, Patrick chose a path of service and enlisted in the United States Navy in 1975 during the Vietnam era. He was assigned to the USNS Voge, an experience that included its collision with a Russian nuclear submarine.
Following his Navy service, Patrick continued his maritime career by enrolling at SUNY Maritime College, where he earned his credentials as a United States Merchant Marine officer. He went on to serve for more than twenty years, spending much of his career at sea and experiencing events few people could ever imagine.
Among his many assignments, Patrick was involved in the difficult and dangerous removal and transportation of mustard gas canisters left in Germany following World War II. Operation Golden Python, oversaw the safe transport and removal of one of the world's largest chemical weapons cachesAfter the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1990.
Later in his career, while serving as a captain with Maersk, Patrick was aboard a Maersk tanker during a hijacking and invasion involving Iranian forces. His service and responsibilities during these and other assignments reflected not only his exceptional seamanship, but also his courage, professionalism, and dedication to the security of his country.
In 1982, Patrick married Melissa Stevens Thompson, also of Niskayuna, New York and they settled in Francestown NH then Peterborough, NH. Together they raised three beloved sons: Conor of Portland, Oregon; Dylan of Keene, New Hampshire; and Ryder of Manhattan, New York.
Although Patrick's career took him around the world, his greatest pride was his family. Much of his life was spent in New Hampshire, where he cherished the years he shared with his sons and family. He was happiest surrounded by the people he loved and took great pride in the men his sons became.
Later in life, Patrick moved to the St. Augustine area and settled on Anastasia Island, where he could be closer to his parents and his surviving brothers, Stephen and Mike.
Patrick was a kind, gentle, and loving man. He possessed a quiet strength, a generous heart, and a deep sense of honor. To those who knew him, he was a devoted father, a loyal friend, and a man who lived a life of service, adventure, and commitment to those he loved.
In keeping with his love of the sea and the life he spent upon it, Patrick will be buried at sea, where his spirit can roam freely over the waters and in a place he loved.
He will be deeply missed, but his spirit will always remain with those who love him.
